title: Video audience acceptance
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for testing whether a video's intended viewers understand it: named audience segments, video-specific tasks such as saying what it does after one viewing, pass criteria fixed before any session, consented sessions a person runs, answers scored by two scorers, a decision that never generalizes beyond the people asked, and every miss turned into a finding about the cut.
boundaries: A person recruits viewers and runs every session; workers plan, score and decide by the fixed criteria.
Viewers are pseudonymous; nothing identifiable is recorded or stored.
Results describe the people asked and this cut only; a missed criterion stays on the record.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for testing whether a video's intended viewers understand it, with pass criteria fixed before any session

value.lets_workers: Plan and score an audience acceptance test of one video: named audience segments, video-specific tasks such as saying what it does after one viewing, recalling a number, naming the next step, reading the AI-voice label or getting the gist with the sound off, pass criteria fixed before the first session, consented sessions a person runs, answers scored against keys by two scorers, a decision that follows from the criteria, and every miss turned into a timestamped finding for the cut.

flow.when: Audiences, tasks, consent and pass criteria, fixed first.
The accountable person agrees to the exact plan version before any session.
A person shows the video and asks, one viewer at a time.
Two scorers mark answers against the keys.
The fixed criteria, applied to the scores.
Each miss and each confusing moment becomes a finding.
The accountable person records go, no-go or go with conditions.
After the fixes, the cut is reviewed again; a new test needs a new plan.

value.worked_example: Synthetic: ten people in two segments watch a fictional pantry's 2:30 film. The criteria were fixed a day before the first session; the decision meets the one-sentence task, misses the next-step and label tasks, leaves the who-is-it-for task unknown because nobody scored it, and proposes four findings: one per miss and one per moment viewers named.
value.complements: The user acceptance testing pack owns criteria agreement and sign-off: this pack uses its agree-criteria and sign-off verbs rather than its own, and adds only what a video needs, one viewing, comprehension tasks with keys and the moments viewers point at. The video review pack judges the cut by rubric; the accessibility audit pack covers the page and player.
provenance_notes: Written for ta-amps's own explainer film, whose review on October 30, 2026 could not say whether a first-time viewer understands what the marketplace does: a question only its intended viewers can answer.

value.rule: Every viewer agrees before the session, from a script read aloud. Viewers are pseudonymous ids; notes paraphrase answers; no face, voice or screen is recorded unless the viewer agrees to that too. No personal data enters a noun.
value.how_it_is_checked: Session notes carry a viewer id and consent true; the plan's consent line names what is and is not recorded.

nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Tasks, keys, audiences and pass criteria are fixed and dated before anyone watches. A criterion changed after seeing answers is a new plan, and the old one's result stands.

nouns.title: Guardrail: the video is tested, not the viewer
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A miss is a fact about the video. No answer is called wrong to the viewer, nobody gets hints, and every miss becomes a finding about the cut at the moment it points to.

nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A handful of viewers says what those people understood from this cut, not what viewers in general do. Shares are reported with their counts, never as percentages of an audience.
value.how_it_is_checked: The decision states the people and cut it applies to, and every share carries its answers and met counts.

nouns.title: Method: one viewing, open questions first, no hints
nouns.category_reason: A short ordered method every session follows, so sessions compare.

steps: Recruit people from each audience segment the video is for; a person does the recruiting.
Read the consent script; start only with a yes.
Show the video once, at normal speed, with sound, on the device the viewer usually watches on; a separate viewer watches muted.
Ask the open tasks first, then the closed ones, in the plan's order, with no hints and no follow-up that teaches the answer.
For confusing or boring moments, let the viewer scrub to the moment and record its time.
Write answers as close to the viewer's words as notes allow.

nouns.title: Task bank: what viewers are asked after one viewing

verbs.title: Plan an audience acceptance test
verbs.summary: Write the plan for one video: audience segments with viewer counts, tasks from the task bank, a muted viewer, the device, a consent line saying what is and is not recorded, and pass criteria per task and segment, dated before any session.

slots.name: video
slots.description: Pin of the video's encoded file media noun.

slots.name: video_brief
slots.description: Pin of the video brief: its audience and point.

slots.name: claim_trace
slots.description: Pin of the video's claim trace, for number recall.

steps: Take the segments from the brief's audience; name each.
Choose tasks that test the brief's point; keep open tasks before closed ones.
Fix and date the pass criteria before any session is booked.
Propose the user acceptance testing pack's agree-criteria for this exact plan version; sessions start only from an agreed version.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.uat-plan's schema.
Every task id is in the task bank.

verbs.title: Run one viewing session
verbs.summary: A person reads the consent script, shows the video once on the viewer's own device, asks the plan's tasks in order without hints, and writes the answers as close to the viewer's words as notes allow.

slots.name: criteria_agreement
slots.description: Pin of the accountable person's agreement to this plan version.

steps: Start only after a yes to the consent script.
Show the video once; ask; let the viewer scrub to any moment they name and note its time.
Keep no recording unless the viewer agreed to one.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.session-notes's schema.

verbs.title: Score the answers against the keys
verbs.summary: Mark every keyed answer met or not against the task bank's keys, with a second scorer, record the scorers' agreement, and copy the open answers as timestamped notes.

slots.name: claim_trace
slots.description: Pin of the claim trace, for number recall.

steps: Score against the key only; a scorer never sees the pass criteria while scoring.
Discuss disagreements and keep both marks' agreement figure.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.scored-answers's schema.
scored_by names at least two scorers, neither the session's runner.
Every keyed answer in the notes has one row.

verbs.title: Apply the fixed criteria
verbs.summary: Apply each pass criterion of the plan to the scored answers: answers, met and share per task and segment, met, missed or unknown, and accepted only when every criterion is met, for these viewers and this cut only.
steps: Compute every share from its counts, rounded to 3 places; a criterion with no answers is unknown.
State who and what the decision applies to.
Propose the user acceptance testing pack's sign-off for the accountable person; the decision itself signs nothing.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.uat-decision's schema.
Recomputing every result from the plan and the scores gives the same values.
The decision's summary passes every check in uat-checks.

verbs.title: Turn misses and confusing moments into findings
verbs.summary: For each missed criterion and each timestamped confusing or boring moment, propose a finding about the cut at that moment with the fix verb the video review pack's routes give, grouped by cause, without enqueueing anything.
steps: Point each miss at the moment of the cut it concerns; a miss with no moment points at the whole cut.
Propose findings-to-fixes record-finding per finding and one fix verb per cause.

acceptance.check: The output validates against the video review pack's fix routing schema.
Every missed criterion and every timed note appears in a group.
